findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:18 — `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at class-definition (module import) time, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` (including all created via `from_integration`) gets the process-start timestamp instead of the time it was created; it must be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`
[Medium/bug] The `test_to_dict` assertion (`queued is not None`) can never fail and masks the incorrect `queued` default

[Medium/data] src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:140 — `assignment_source.to_dict()` embeds a `datetime` (`queued`) directly into the Celery `apply_async` kwargs; datetimes are not JSON-serializable under a JSON-based serializer, so dispatch raises and breaks the whole inbound→outbound assignee sync path
[Medium/data] Where a custom encoder coerces the `queued` datetime to a string, `from_dict` never parses it back, so the reconstructed object violates its declared `datetime` type

[Medium/api] src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:~401 — the abstract `sync_assignee_outbound` was not updated to declare `assignment_source`, yet src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:60-62 now invokes it with `assignment_source=`; implementations only receive it implicitly via `**kwargs` (silently ignored, so no provider can act on it), and any subclass that implements the declared abstract signature exactly (without `**kwargs`) will raise `TypeError` at runtime

[Low/api] src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:411 — `sync_status_outbound` gained an `assignment_source` parameter, but no caller in the codebase passes it and `should_sync("outbound_status")` is never invoked with a source, so status-sync cycle/echo suppression is not actually implemented; this is dead API surface that implies protection that doesn't exist

[Medium/test_gap] tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py — no test covers the complementary half of the guard: that outbound assignee sync still fires for a *different* integration when `assignment_source` is set; an over-broad guard such as `if sync_source: return False` would pass the entire suite (source is `None` in the legacy tests and matches in the new one)

[Low/test_gap] The real cycle entry point is untested: nothing exercises `sync_group_assignee_inbound` → `GroupAssignee.objects.assign/deassign(assignment_source=...)` → task `assignment_source_dict` round-trip, nor the inbound deassign path; existing tests only call `GroupAssignee.objects.assign` directly with an in-memory source, so the `to_dict`/`from_dict` round-trip through the broker (bypassed by the inline task runner) has zero coverage

[Low/bug] src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:390 — the suppression is per-integration, not per linked issue: `sync_group_assignee_outbound` fans out to every linked external issue, and the guard blocks the *entire* installation when the source integration matches; for a group linked to multiple external issues on the same integration, an inbound change from one issue suppresses propagation to the others, so their assignees silently drift

[Low/data] src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:30-35 — `from_dict` does no type validation and returns `None` on malformed input, which the task treats as 'no source', so cycle protection fails open silently (no logging) instead of failing closed; garbage-typed dicts (e.g., `integration_id` as a string) produce instances whose `integration_id` equality check in `should_sync` never matches, bypassing the guard

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] The `test_to_dict` assertion (`queued is not None`) can never fail and masks the incorrect `queued` default

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource`, the dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` evaluates `timezone.now()` once at import/class definition time, so all instances created without an explicit `queued` share the same timestamp (should be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`). The test `test_to_dict` only asserts `queued is not None`, which will always pass as long as a datetime exists, and thus fails to catch the incorrect default behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] Where a custom encoder coerces the `queued` datetime to a string, `from_dict` never parses it back, so the reconstructed object violates its declared `datetime` type

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource`, `to_dict()` uses `asdict(self)` which includes `queued` (a `datetime`) and this dict is passed through Celery `apply_async` as `assignment_source_dict` (see `sync_group_assignee_outbound` → `sync_assignee_outbound`). `from_dict()` reconstructs via `cls(**input_dict)` and does not parse/normalize `queued` at all, so if task serialization coerces datetimes to strings, the reconstructed object would have `queued` as a `str` despite the `datetime` annotation. The diff doesn’t show the serializer/encoder behavior, and `queued` isn’t used elsewhere here, so this is a robustness/type-consistency issue rather than a clearly verifiable runtime defect in this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:~401 — the abstract `sync_assignee_outbound` was not updated to declare `assignment_source`, yet src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:60-62 now invokes it with `assignment_source=`; implementations only receive it implicitly via `**kwargs` (silently ignored, so no provider can act on it), and any subclass that implements the declared abstract signature exactly (without `**kwargs`) will raise `TypeError` at runtime

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new `assignment_source` concept threaded through outbound assignee syncing: `sync_assignee_outbound` task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)` (src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py). In contrast, in the integration mixin (src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py) only `should_sync` and `sync_status_outbound` were updated to accept an `AssignmentSource`; there is no corresponding visible update for the `sync_assignee_outbound` method signature in that mixin section (it remains the same block that ends in `raise NotImplementedError`). This creates a real interface mismatch risk: any concrete integration implementation whose `sync_assignee_outbound` does not accept the new kwarg will raise `TypeError` when the task passes `assignment_source=`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:411 — `sync_status_outbound` gained an `assignment_source` parameter, but no caller in the codebase passes it and `should_sync("outbound_status")` is never invoked with a source, so status-sync cycle/echo suppression is not actually implemented; this is dead API surface that implies protection that doesn't exist

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly adds an optional `assignment_source`/`sync_source` plumbing point (e.g., `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source=...)` and the abstract `sync_status_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)`), but only the assignee outbound path is actually updated to parse/pass an `AssignmentSource` (`sync_assignee_outbound` task -> `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)` and `sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)`). No corresponding diff shows any caller passing `assignment_source` into `sync_status_outbound` or invoking `should_sync` for status with a source, so status echo/cycle suppression is not implemented by the changes shown. This isn’t a verifiable functional bug in the diff by itself (the new params are optional/defaulted), but it is incomplete/unused API surface that could misleadingly suggest parity with the assignee suppression behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py — no test covers the complementary half of the guard: that outbound assignee sync still fires for a *different* integration when `assignment_source` is set; an over-broad guard such as `if sync_source: return False` would pass the entire suite (source is `None` in the legacy tests and matches in the new one)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new nontrivial guard logic in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source)` to prevent cycles only when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` (src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py). Tests cover (a) `assignment_source=None` still syncs (`assert_called_with(... assignment_source=None)`) and (b) matching integration source does not sync (`assert_not_called`). There is no test asserting that syncing still occurs when `assignment_source` is provided but refers to a *different* integration, so an overly broad guard like `if sync_source: return False` could pass the shown suite despite breaking intended behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] The real cycle entry point is untested: nothing exercises `sync_group_assignee_inbound` → `GroupAssignee.objects.assign/deassign(assignment_source=...)` → task `assignment_source_dict` round-trip, nor the inbound deassign path; existing tests only call `GroupAssignee.objects.assign` directly with an in-memory source, so the `to_dict`/`from_dict` round-trip through the broker (bypassed by the inline task runner) has zero coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new inbound entry path `sync_group_assignee_inbound()` that now calls `GroupAssignee.objects.assign/deassign(..., assignment_source=AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration))`, and outbound propagation now serializes via `assignment_source.to_dict()` into the celery task kwarg `assignment_source_dict`, which is parsed by `AssignmentSource.from_dict()` in `sync_assignee_outbound`. The added/updated tests in `tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py` exercise `GroupAssignee.objects.assign/deassign` directly, and do not cover the full inbound flow through `sync_group_assignee_inbound` (including the inbound deassign branch). Also, while one test passes a non-None `assignment_source` (thus likely executing the `to_dict`/`from_dict` path), there is no assertion validating the parsed source passed into the installation call, and the inbound entrypoint itself remains untested. This is a concrete test coverage gap for newly added nontrivial behavior, not a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:390 — the suppression is per-integration, not per linked issue: `sync_group_assignee_outbound` fans out to every linked external issue, and the guard blocks the *entire* installation when the source integration matches; for a group linked to multiple external issues on the same integration, an inbound change from one issue suppresses propagation to the others, so their assignees silently drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a guard in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source)` that returns `False` whenever `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` (issues.py). Outbound assignee sync fans out per linked `ExternalIssue` in `sync_group_assignee_outbound` (utils/sync.py), but the same `AssignmentSource` (only integration-level, no external_issue identifier) is passed to every queued `sync_assignee_outbound` task. Therefore, when an inbound assignment originates from integration X, every outbound assignee sync to *any* linked external issue on integration X will be suppressed, including other linked issues besides the one that originated the change. This matches the finding’s “per-integration, not per linked issue” suppression and can cause linked issues within the same integration to drift.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:30-35 — `from_dict` does no type validation and returns `None` on malformed input, which the task treats as 'no source', so cycle protection fails open silently (no logging) instead of failing closed; garbage-typed dicts (e.g., `integration_id` as a string) produce instances whose `integration_id` equality check in `should_sync` never matches, bypassing the guard

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds cycle protection in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync()` by comparing `sync_source.integration_id` to `self.org_integration.integration_id`. However, `AssignmentSource.from_dict()` (new file) simply does `return cls(**input_dict)` with no runtime type enforcement; dataclass annotations aren’t validated. If `assignment_source_dict` contains `integration_id` as a string (or other wrong type), `from_dict` will still return an `AssignmentSource` whose `integration_id` is not an `int`, causing the equality check to fail and the cycle guard to be bypassed. Additionally, malformed dicts return `None`, which the task treats as “no source” and thus also bypasses the guard (fail-open).
